overview: The Etruscans lived in a network of central Italian city-states. Metalworking, imported luxury materials and distinctive funerary art reveal communities deeply involved in Mediterranean exchange.

items.text: Bucchero pottery has a glossy black surface and often uses shapes associated with metal vessels.
Bronze workers made decorated chariots, vessels, mirrors and sculpture. Access to copper and iron supported their craft traditions.
Greek painted pottery was highly valued in Etruria. Trade also brought ivory, amber and other materials used by local artists.
At Cerveteri, rock-cut tombs reproduce features of houses. Their arrangement into streets and small squares offers clues to settlement planning.
Painted tombs at Tarquinia preserve scenes of living, dying and religious belief. Funerary images provide evidence that short surviving inscriptions often cannot supply.
Roman expansion absorbed the Etruscan cities over time. Their culture did not end on the map's current 323 BCE snapshot boundary.
